turns.content: How does a turbidity sensor physically take its reading?

must_contain: a light source illuminates the sample and a detector measures the light scattered at a 90-degree angle
multiparameter sondes typically use a near-infrared source (about 780–900 nm), usually an LED, with one detector at 90 degrees
the result is reported in nephelometric turbidity units (NTU)
must_not: describes an optical arrangement absent from the corpus
confuses the turbidity sensor with the optical DO sensor

turns.content: Does that explain why NTU and FNU differ?

must_contain: links the light source to the unit — white light corresponds to NTU, infrared to FNU
restates that the two units are not interchangeable
must_not: supplies a conversion between the units
